title: Who is DTI exec Ceferino Rodolfo?
summary: Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo of DTI"s Industry Development and Investment Promotions Group took the witness stand on Friday, November 20, for the 45th day of…

blocks.text: Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) Undersecretary Ceferino Rodolfo of DTI’s Industry Development and Investment Promotions Group took the witness stand on Friday, November 20, for the 45th day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte.
Rodolfo, who also serves as the Managing Head of the Board of Investments, has been with the DTI since March 2013 when he was appointed Assistant Secretary.
Rodolfo was promoted to DTI Undersecretary in February 2016, a position he has held since.
Rodolfo will testify on business registration Cale88 Foods Corporation, a declared business interest of Atty. Manases Carpio, husband of the Vice President.

The defense team is offering Rodolfo’s testimony to prove that Cale88 Foods Corporation is a duly registered export enterprise with the BOI and is engaged in the lawful and legitimate business of producing and exporting Banana Chips.

Rodolfo’s testimony is also being offered to prove that he issued Cale88 Foods Corporation's Certificate of Registration No. 2021-186 as an Export Enterprise engaged in PSIC 10309 Manufacture of Foods Products, Export of Producer of Banana Chips.

Prosecution witness and financial forensic expert Alex Cabrera, an accountant-lawyer, earlier testified that the Vice President and her husband have unexplained wealth worth P817 million to P1.5 billion due to non-declaration of their assets in their joint Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth (SALN), including income from Cale88 Foods Corporation.

Defense witness and AML Consulting PH head, Atty. Rainer Dela Fuente, earlier testified that there were red flags in Cale88 Foods Corporation operations given that the firm only has two employees, received P319 million remittances from China and recorded 757 covered transactions and suspicious transactions worth P1.2 billion.
Dela Fuente, however, said such red flags are not automatically illegal. —VAL, GMA News
